name: Ethnographic Synthesis
title: Ethnographic Synthesis
answer: Ethnographic synthesis is the work of drawing together findings from two or more ethnographic or closely observational studies into a single comparative account. It deals with fieldnotes, interview transcripts, documents and researcher memos, and it treats culture, context and meaning as data rather than as background. The unit of interest is usually a concept, a practice or a setting rather than a single participant, so the synthesis asks how an idea travels across sites and how it changes shape when it does. It sits inside qualitative evidence synthesis and mixed methods work, and it is often reached for when a decision needs a richer account than a list of themes can give.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Ethnographic synthesis is the work of drawing together findings from two or more ethnographic or closely observational studies into a single comparative account. It deals with fieldnotes, interview transcripts, documents and researcher memos, and it treats culture, context and meaning as data rather than as background. The unit of interest is usually a concept, a practice or a setting rather than a single participant, so the synthesis asks how an idea travels across sites and how it changes shape when it does. It sits inside qualitative evidence synthesis and mixed methods work, and it is often reached for when a decision needs a richer account than a list of themes can give.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on qualitative data analysis software such as NVivo, ATLAS.ti, MAXQDA or Dedoose, which hold coded excerpts, memos and the links between them. Teams also rely on shared codebooks, reference managers, secure file storage and transcription services, plus a version control habit for the codebook itself. Where primary studies are published, the synthesis team needs the full text and often the appendices, not just the abstract. Some groups now add language models to help screen large result sets or to suggest candidate codes, but the coded excerpt and its source stay the unit of record.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The usual sequence is a documented search, then close reading of each included study to extract its own concepts and the author's interpretations of them. Those extracts are compared across studies, and concepts that appear to match are translated into one another rather than simply pooled, which is where the interpretive weight of the synthesis sits. A second reader checks a sample of the coding, disagreements are resolved in the open, and the reasoning is kept in an audit trail so a reader can follow how a claim was reached. Reflexivity matters here, because the synthesist's own field experience and assumptions shape which comparisons look obvious.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Ethical handling centres on consent, anonymisation and the risk that a quote plus a setting description can identify a person in a small community. Data sharing agreements, ethics approvals and the terms attached to the original studies all constrain what can be reused and how it can be quoted. Provenance is the other half of the problem, since a synthesis is only as good as the studies under it, and a claim that has drifted from its source is hard to trace back. On this site, content links to the original paper rather than to a search tool, which keeps that chain visible.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward living or updateable syntheses that are refreshed as new studies appear, rather than one-off reviews that age quietly. Machine assistance is spreading into screening, deduplication and first-pass coding, which shifts the human effort toward judgement about translation and context. At the same time there is more pressure for transparent reporting, published codebooks and open audit trails, so that a reader can see how the interpretation was built. Shared qualitative data archives are growing, though access conditions and consent terms still limit how far reuse can go.
